Nixon ended American involvement in Vietnam combat in 1973 and the [military draft](Conscription_in_the_United_States "Conscription in the United States") in the same year. His [visit to China](1972_visit_by_Richard_Nixon_to_China "1972 visit by Richard Nixon to China") in 1972 eventually led to [diplomatic relations between the two nations](Joint_Communiqu%C3%A9_on_the_Establishment_of_Diplomatic_Relations "Joint Communiqué on the Establishment of Diplomatic Relations"), and he also then concluded the [Anti-Ballistic Missile Treaty](Anti-Ballistic_Missile_Treaty "Anti-Ballistic Missile Treaty") with the Soviet Union. Domestically, Nixon pushed for the [Controlled Substances Act](Controlled_Substances_Act "Controlled Substances Act") and began the [war on drugs](War_on_drugs "War on drugs"). Nixon's first term took place at the height of the American [environmental movement](Environmental_movement_in_the_United_States "Environmental movement in the United States") and enacted many progressive environmental policy shifts; his administration created the [Environmental Protection Agency](United_States_Environmental_Protection_Agency "United States Environmental Protection Agency") and passed legislation such as the [Endangered Species Act](Endangered_Species_Act_of_1973 "Endangered Species Act of 1973"), the [Clean Air Acts](Clean_Air_Act_(United_States) "Clean Air Act (United States)"), and the [Clean Water Acts](Clean_Water_Act "Clean Water Act") (although he vetoed the final version of the CWA). He implemented the recently ratified [Twenty-sixth Amendment](Twenty-sixth_Amendment_to_the_United_States_Constitution "Twenty-sixth Amendment to the United States Constitution"), which lowered the voting age from 21 to 18 and enforced the [desegregation](Desegregation_busing "Desegregation busing") of Southern schools. Under Nixon, relations with Native Americans improved, seeing an increase in [self-determination](Native_American_self-determination "Native American self-determination") for [Native Americans](Native_American_policy_of_the_Richard_Nixon_administration "Native American policy of the Richard Nixon administration") and his administration rescinded the [termination policy](Indian_termination_policy "Indian termination policy"). In his second term, Nixon ordered [an airlift](Operation_Nickel_Grass "Operation Nickel Grass") to resupply Israeli losses in the [Yom Kippur War](Yom_Kippur_War "Yom Kippur War"), a conflict which led to the [oil crisis](1973_oil_crisis "1973 oil crisis") at home. Nixon](Francis_A._Nixon "Francis A. Nixon"). His mother was a <Quaker>, and his father converted from <Methodism> to the Quaker faith. ## Democratic Party
- **Presidential Nominee: John F. Kennedy** - **United States Navy**
  - Served during World War II as Lieutenant, commanding PT-109 in the Pacific theater
  - Awarded Navy and Marine Corps Medal for heroism

- **Vice-Presidential Nominee: Lyndon B. Johnson** - **United States Navy**
  - Served from 1941-1942 (active) and 1942-1964 (reserve)
  - Achieved the rank of Commander
  - Awarded the Silver Star for service in the Salamaua-Lae campaign

## Republican Party
- **Presidential Nominee: Richard Nixon** - **United States Navy**
  - Served from 1942-1946 (active) and 1946-1966 (inactive)
  - Achieved the rank of Commander
  - Served in the Pacific War during World War II
  - Awarded Navy and Marine Corps Commendation Medal

- **Vice-Presidential Nominee: Henry Cabot Lodge Jr.** - **United States Army**
  - Served during World War II, resigning from the Senate in 1944
  - Achieved the rank of Lieutenant Colonel (later rose to Major General in the reserves)
  - Served in Italy and France, including the Battle of Gazala
